observation_summary: The application throws a RuntimeException when comparing objects that have a faulty equals() implementation, even when the objects being compared are the same instance.
hypothesis: The equality check logic in Equality.areEqual() fails to handle the case where the two objects are the same reference before proceeding to call their potentially buggy equals() methods.
prediction: Adding a reference equality check (o1 == o2) at the beginning of the areEqual method will prevent the code from invoking the faulty equals() method on the same object instance, thus avoiding the exception.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the addition of an 'if (o1 == o2) return true;' guard clause at the start of the areEqual method. This confirms that the root cause was a missing validation check for reference equality.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic missing guard condition. The code was attempting to perform equality checks on objects without first verifying if they were the same reference, which caused issues when the objects' own equals() methods were unreliable. Adding the reference equality check is a textbook example of a 'Checking' fix.
evidence_used: The stack trace shows a RuntimeException originating from a custom equals() method during an equality check.
The fix diff shows the addition of a guard clause: 'if (o1 == o2) { return true; }'.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not a rewrite of the comparison algorithm itself, but rather the addition of a guard condition to bypass the algorithm when unnecessary.
